To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
recA(Sfr) and recA441(TiF) suppress the deficiency in repair of UV-induced damage of recF mutants in a recJ+ strain and that recJ+ can be used for repair in a recF- background.
recA(SRF) mutations, which suppress the recF phenotype, are selected in recB+ recF+ cells, and that recJ is required to suppress recF.
recA(SRF) and recA(441) suppress the UV sensitivity of a recF mutant only in a recJ+ background.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a new aspect of the regulation of the recF pathway.
the role of the recF gene and the recA gene in the postreplication repair pathway of Escherichlia coli.
the role of RecF protein in recombination and repair and with its relationship to the RecJ protein.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the suppression of the UV-sensitive phenotypes of recF mutants by the recA(Srf), recA(Tif), and recA441 mutations requires recJ+, whereas the suppression of recF mutants in the uvrA background by the recA441 and recA(Srf)(leu) mutations does not.
recF and recJ+ function in a single pathway of postreplication repair.
the recF pathway and the recA-dependent pathway of recombination/repair can be functionally independent of each other.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
recA(SRF) and recA(SRF+) are recF independent and that the suppression of the recF defect is recJ dependent.
recA(SRF) is a new member in the group of recF-independent genes.
the recF pathway is not the only one for postreplication repair and that the recJ+ product is required for this pathway.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the recJ gene is required for the recF pathway in recombination and repair.
the suppression of a recF mutant phenotype by mutations in recA requires the recJ gene product.
the recF gene product is not essential for the recJ-dependent postreplication repair pathway.
